pubchem.title: (-)-Caryophyllene
pubchem.description: (-)-beta-caryophyllene is a beta-caryophyllene in which the stereocentre adjacent to the exocyclic double bond has S configuration while the remaining stereocentre has R configuration. It is the most commonly occurring form of beta-caryophyllene, occurring in many essential oils, particularly oil of cloves. It has a role as an insect attractant, a metabolite, a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drug and a fragrance. It is an enantiomer of a (+)-beta-caryophyllene.

studies.title: Topical Use of 20% Beta Caryophyllene Alone And In Combination With 0.025% Capsaicin for Pain Caused by Osteoarthritis Of The Knee
studies.summary:
This study consists of a randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled crossover trial with open label extension evaluating a topical natural health cream containing ß-caryophyllene alone and in combination with 0.025% capsicum oleoresin against placebo. At the end of the randomized controlled phase of the trial all participants will be given open-label combination cream to be administered over the subsequent 3 weeks.

Primary Endpoint: Evaluation of improvement in pain interference as measured by the BPI in individuals who are experiencing pain due to osteoarthritis of the knee.

studies.summary: Beta-Caryophyllene is an essential oil and cannabis plant derivative also found in edible herbs. It has shown promise as a potential analgesic in preclinical trials. However, there are no human studies characterizing pharmacokinetics of BCP in humans. Therefore, it is of great importance to determine the pharmacokinetics of BCP in humans so that appropriate dosing can be developed for analgesia. This pharmacokinetic work will lay the groundwork for subsequent experiments testing the neural mechanism of BCP on pain.

consumer_summary.what_it_is: β-Caryophyllene is a naturally occurring terpene responsible for the warm, woody, and spicy aromas in many essential oils. It is widely used as a fragrance and flavor compound, giving a distinctive peppery bite to familiar spices. You encounter it every time you smell crushed cloves or enjoy heavily spiced foods.
consumer_summary.found_in: This molecule is abundant in everyday botanicals like rosemary, oregano, thyme, and holy basil. It is also a key component in hops, carrots, and various citrus fruits like lemon and mandarin.
consumer_summary.why_researchers_care: Researchers are fascinated by β-caryophyllene because it acts directly on the body's endocannabinoid system, specifically targeting the CB2 receptor without causing psychoactive effects. This unique mechanism has sparked intense interest in its potential as a non-steroidal anti-inflammatory and neuroprotective agent. The strongest evidence so far comes from human observational studies (Oxford level 2b), which are exploring how this dietary terpene might influence oxidative stress and cellular health.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Researchers are exploring whether β-caryophyllene's interaction with CB2 receptors can provide meaningful pain relief.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: This is currently being tested in humans, such as in the active clinical trial NCT04451863 evaluating the analgesic effects of terpenes.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Observational data has led researchers to ask whether this terpene might play a role in cellular defense and cancer biology.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: To move beyond observational associations, researchers would need to design a randomized, placebo-controlled clinical trial measuring tumor markers and progression in patients receiving standardized doses alongside standard care.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: Early animal work points toward a potential role in supporting focus and memory, raising the question of whether it could protect cognitive function over time.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: The next step would be a phase 1 human clinical trial giving a standardized oral dose to healthy adults and measuring memory retention and attention span over several weeks.

hypothesized_benefits.hypothesis: If early findings bear out, this molecule might help regulate stress pathways and promote a sense of calm.
hypothesized_benefits.study_to_test_it: A randomized, double-blind clinical trial in adults with generalized anxiety, measuring subjective stress scores and cortisol levels over an eight-week period, would definitively test this.

consumer_summary.cautions: In industrial or occupational settings, concentrated exposure to β-caryophyllene has been recorded as a hazard for allergic contact dermatitis.
consumer_summary.evidence_at_a_glance: Best evidence so far includes human observational work and early clinical trials (Oxford level 2b); most of the rest is animal and lab research.
